tasks.short: Keep AFAS customer balances, payment promises and collection notes up to date.

today.trigger: A customer replies, a collection call ends, or a payment or dispute changes the account position.
steps: Open the customer account and outstanding invoices in AFAS.
Read the Outlook conversation or review call notes.
Record the collection action, customer explanation and any promised payment date.
Update the follow-up date and flag disputes or financial concerns.
drudgery: Copying invoice references and dates between systems.
Rewriting email threads as account notes.
Checking whether a colleague already recorded the same event.
today.time_sinks: Repeated lookup and entry across AFAS and Outlook; incomplete notes cause later rereading.

lenses.faster: Extract invoice references, promises and dispute reasons from messages, then validate them against AFAS. Copying and most note writing disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new message or posted payment triggers an account update. Ambiguous customer matches and conflicting promises enter an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a complete, dated collection history for every account and measure how often promised payments actually arrive.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive administration so I can spend more time understanding customers and resolving difficult accounts.
lenses.options: Show competing interpretations when a message could describe a payment promise, a dispute or an unsupported claim.
lenses.altitude: I own the collection-note rules and review recurring errors instead of typing every update.
reach: Prepare receivables movement explanations for the Controller.
Supply evidenced payment promises to the FP&A Analyst's cash forecast.

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a customer's explanation signals a genuine commercial problem, and distinguishing their claim from a verified fact.
tasks.pattern_why: Messages need interpretation, but account identifiers, amounts and dates can be checked by deterministic rules before a structured note is saved.

in_practice.trigger: A message reaches the collections mailbox, a short call note is submitted, or an AFAS payment event is detected.
steps: Match the event to a customer and invoice using approved identifiers.
Extract the action, claimed payment, promise date and dispute reason with source references.
Validate amounts and dates against current AFAS records, keeping customer claims separate from confirmed receipts.
Save routine notes through an authorised AFAS connector and route uncertainty for review.
Check that each event was recorded once and report failed writes.
in_practice.human_gate: Review uncertain matches and financial-status interpretations; credit limits, write-offs and legal actions require separate approval.
systems: AFAS Profit with an authorised custom dossier type and connector
data_needed: Relevant messages and submitted call notes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS customer dossier plus a restricted integration log containing source ID, extracted fields, validation outcome and write result.

evidence.claim: AFAS KnSubject supports creating dossier items with attachments; the proposed collection-note type and permissions still need configuration.
Extracting structured promises and dispute reasons from messages is plausible when outputs are checked against source records.
The 70% labour saving and 3x processing speedup are planning hypotheses, not measured Noordhaven results.

risks: A customer's statement that payment was sent could be incorrectly recorded as confirmed cash.
Messages may contain misleading instructions; message content must never control connector permissions or workflow rules.

Customer financial information needs restricted access and a defined retention policy under AVG/GDPR. [AP retention guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/nl/over-privacy/persoonsgegevens/bewaren-van-persoonsgegevens)
research_questions: What proportion of collection events can be matched to one AFAS customer and invoice without manual interpretation?
Can the required custom dossier fields be written and retrieved with the available AFAS permissions?
Does a sampled pilot preserve every material promise and dispute without inventing financial facts?

tasks.short: Find overdue invoices and decide which customer accounts need attention today.

today.trigger: The daily collections review starts, an invoice becomes overdue, or a payment promise expires.
steps: Retrieve outstanding invoices and payment terms from AFAS.
Compare balances with the nightly Power BI dashboard and any recent receipts.
Check disputes, payment promises and previous contact.
Rank accounts and create the day's follow-up list.
drudgery: Sorting and filtering ageing exports.
Removing paid or disputed invoices from working lists.
Reconstructing why an account was prioritised yesterday.
today.time_sinks: Reconciling a nightly dashboard with newer payments and manually combining balances with collection history.

lenses.faster: Calculate ageing and refresh the work queue directly from AFAS. Spreadsheet preparation disappears, leaving priority exceptions to judge.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled run identifies newly overdue invoices and broken promises, then removes accounts once payments are posted.
lenses.ambitious: Monitor the whole portfolio consistently and show which overdue balances threaten the cash forecast before month end.
lenses.joy: Replace list maintenance with focused investigation of accounts where intervention could make a difference.
lenses.options: Compare queues ranked by overdue value, broken promises, dispute age or customer concentration.
lenses.altitude: I design and test prioritisation rules, then adjust them using collection outcomes.
reach: Provide the FP&A Analyst with an explained cash-at-risk view.
Prepare aged-receivables evidence for the Controller's month-close review.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when an important customer, operational failure or unusual dispute deserves attention beyond its numerical rank.
tasks.pattern_why: Due dates, balances, promises and policy thresholds support an explainable rules-based queue; a model is unnecessary for the core calculation.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled AFAS refresh completes or a payment promise reaches its deadline.
steps: Read open items, contractual due dates and collection statuses from AFAS with a visible refresh timestamp.
Calculate ageing and flag broken promises, unresolved disputes and missing data.
Apply approved priority rules and produce an explained work queue.
Let the officer reorder exceptional accounts and record the reason.
Publish aggregate ageing and cash-risk movements for the nightly Power BI refresh.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer handles priority exceptions; a queue position cannot itself change credit terms or stop service.
systems: AFAS Profit through authorised read connectors
data_needed: Open invoices, due dates and currencies
Approved priority rules and customer relationships
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted collections queue history with source timestamp, ranking reasons and manual overrides; aggregate results in Power BI.

evidence.claim: AFAS exposes reminder history through outstanding items, supporting investigation of previous collection activity.
Ageing calculations and transparent prioritisation can run as deterministic software.
The 60% labour saving and 2.5x speedup depend on reliable statuses and access to fresher AFAS data.

risks: The nightly Power BI extract can miss today's receipts; action queues need current AFAS checks and visible timestamps.
Ranking only by balance can neglect small but serious disputes.

Extending the queue into AI creditworthiness assessment of natural persons, potentially including sole traders, needs a separate EU AI Act assessment. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)
research_questions: Can AFAS provide sufficiently fresh open items and receipt data for the daily queue?
Are disputes and promises recorded consistently enough to drive rules?
Does the proposed ranking identify more recoverable cash than the officer's current queue?

tasks.short: Contact overdue customers with the right invoice details and ask when they will pay.

today.trigger: An invoice reaches a reminder stage or a customer misses an agreed payment date.
steps: Check the balance, recent receipts and dispute status in AFAS.
Find the customer's accounts-payable contact and previous correspondence.
Prepare an email or letter, or call the customer.
Ask for payment or a specific payment date.
Record the outcome and schedule follow-up.
drudgery: Assembling invoice lists and attachments.
Rewriting standard reminders.
Chasing invalid email addresses and logging contact attempts.
today.time_sinks: Preparing each contact and checking that a reminder is still justified immediately before sending.

lenses.faster: Prepare a checked invoice pack, reminder draft and call brief in one place. Repeated searches and routine drafting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Approved standard reminders can run on a schedule for undisputed accounts, with payment and contact checks immediately before sending.
lenses.ambitious: Give every overdue customer timely, accurate follow-up and measure responses by reminder stage and channel.
lenses.joy: Spend less time composing repetitive emails and more time having useful conversations with customer finance teams.
lenses.options: Offer concise Dutch and English drafts plus a call approach suited to the account's history.
lenses.altitude: I manage reminder policy, contact quality and outcomes across the portfolio.
reach: Improve customer billing-contact quality with accounts receivable.
Identify recurring invoice-delivery problems for the Bookkeepers.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing tone, timing and personal contact when a relationship or disputed delivery makes a routine reminder inappropriate.
tasks.pattern_why: Contact preparation spans balances, messages and attachments; each nonstandard communication needs a person to check its accuracy and commercial effect.

in_practice.trigger: An account reaches a configured reminder stage or breaks a payment promise.
steps: Retrieve current balances, contact details, disputes and prior reminders.
Apply suppression rules for unresolved disputes, recent receipts and agreed contact pauses.
Prepare a verified invoice pack and an approved-template reminder or call brief.
Obtain approval for nonstandard wording and recheck the balance immediately before dispatch.
Send through the approved channel and record delivery, replies and the next action.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve each nonstandard message; calls and visits stay with the officer. Standard reminders may move to exception-only supervision after validation.
data_needed: Approved wording, cadence and suppression rules
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS customer dossier with the exact communication, recipient, balance-check time and approval; dispatch status in the workflow log.

evidence.claim: AFAS records reminder history against debtor accounts and exposes it through outstanding items.
Preparing grounded reminder drafts and call briefs is plausible; Noordhaven's approval and dispatch workflow would need configuration.
The 35% labour saving and 1.4x contact-cycle speedup are estimates; they do not imply customers pay 1.4x sooner.

risks: A payment arriving between preparation and dispatch could produce an incorrect reminder.
Incorrect recipients or attachments could expose another customer's financial information.

Consumer and business reminder requirements differ; legal wording and fees need approved rules for the actual debtor type. [RVO payment guidance](https://ondernemersplein.overheid.nl/wetten-en-regels/betalingstermijn-incassokosten-en-wettelijke-rente/)
research_questions: What proportion of contacts are standard reminders rather than disputes or relationship-sensitive calls?
Can current AFAS configuration support suppression and a final balance check before dispatch?
Does a pilot reduce preparation time without increasing incorrect reminders or complaints?

tasks.short: Explain customer account balances, payment allocations and invoice problems.

today.trigger: A customer emails or calls about an invoice, missing payment, credit note or disputed balance.
steps: Identify the customer and the account question.
Check invoices, receipts, allocations and credit notes in AFAS.
Read earlier correspondence and request missing operational evidence.
Explain the position or arrange investigation with the responsible colleague.
Record the answer, owner and next action.
drudgery: Searching long email threads.
Recreating account statements and invoice packs.
Forwarding questions repeatedly to find an owner.
today.time_sinks: Finding the evidence behind a balance and waiting for delivery, pricing or damage-claim information.

lenses.faster: Assemble the relevant ledger entries and correspondence, then draft an answer with evidence links.
lenses.autonomous: Verified requests for invoice copies and simple balance explanations can receive standard responses. Disputes and uncertain identities go to the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Track every query to an owner and use recurring causes to prevent invoice errors across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repeated explanations, leaving investigation and useful customer service.
lenses.options: Show possible explanations such as an unallocated receipt, partial payment or pending credit, with evidence for each.
lenses.altitude: I improve account-query resolution rules and fix recurring causes with billing and operations.
reach: Lead receivables dispute tracking for the Bookkeepers.
Provide recurring billing-error analysis to the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Resolving conflicting evidence and accepting responsibility for an explanation when the ledger and the customer's experience disagree.
tasks.pattern_why: The model classifies questions and explains retrieved facts; deterministic controls verify identity, balances and permitted response types.

in_practice.trigger: A customer question arrives in the collections mailbox.
steps: Verify the sender against approved contacts and identify the customer account.
Classify the request and retrieve relevant current AFAS entries and authorised documents.
Calculate balances in software and draft an explanation tied to those entries.
Send only approved low-risk response types automatically; route disputes and missing evidence to a named owner.
Record the answer and follow the case until resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves disputed, ambiguous or commercially sensitive answers; credits, refunds and allocation changes follow separate approval controls.
systems: Proposed query classification and response workflow
data_needed: Invoices, receipts, credit notes and allocation history
Approved answer types and escalation owners
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS customer dossier and a restricted query register with evidence references, response text, owner and resolution status.

evidence.claim: Grounded drafting can accelerate repetitive account explanations when calculations and source access are controlled.
AFAS supports adding dossier records and attachments through KnSubject, providing a possible record of query handling.
The 55% labour saving and 2x resolution speedup assume a substantial share of simple queries; operational disputes may see little elapsed-time improvement.

risks: A fluent explanation could conceal an incorrect allocation or an unsupported assumption.
Proof of delivery and warehouse evidence sources were not supplied; the workflow cannot assume access to a transport or warehouse system.
An unverified sender could obtain invoices or account information.
research_questions: What share of questions can be answered completely from AFAS and existing correspondence?
Where are delivery records, warehouse charges and damage evidence stored, and who can authorise access?
Which response types can pass identity and factual checks reliably enough for automatic sending?
Does the pilot shorten full resolution time, including handoffs to operations?

tasks.short: Agree credible payment commitments with overdue customers and resolve barriers to payment.

today.trigger: Routine reminders fail, a customer requests instalments, or a significant invoice remains unpaid.
steps: Review the balance, previous promises and any disputed logistics charges.
Discuss what prevents payment with the customer.
Propose payment dates or instalments within delegated authority.
Seek approval for concessions or arrangements outside that authority.
Confirm the agreement and monitor whether payments arrive.
drudgery: Reconstructing account history before calls.
Calculating instalment schedules.
Writing confirmations and checking promised dates.
today.time_sinks: Preparation, internal approvals and repeated conversations after promises are broken.

lenses.faster: Prepare a concise negotiation brief and calculate permitted payment schedules before the call.
lenses.autonomous: Monitor approved arrangements and flag missed instalments automatically. Negotiation and concessions remain human decisions.
lenses.ambitious: Assess every material arrangement against its cash impact and track which agreements actually hold.
lenses.joy: Keep the relationship work and problem solving while removing calculations and repetitive follow-up administration.
lenses.options: Compare immediate partial payment, dated full payment and instalment scenarios, showing timing and remaining exposure.
lenses.altitude: I improve negotiation policy using outcomes and recurring reasons for nonpayment.
reach: Supply payment-arrangement scenarios to FP&A.
Prepare evidence for the Controller's doubtful-debt assessment.

tasks.human_edge: Building trust, testing whether a promise is credible and balancing recovery against a valuable commercial relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Preparation and scenario calculations are checkable, but persuasion, concessions and commitments require a person with delegated authority.

in_practice.trigger: The officer selects an account for a negotiation call.
steps: Assemble a sourced brief covering balances, disputes and previous promises.
Calculate policy-compliant payment scenarios and their cash timing.
Let the officer lead the conversation and choose an arrangement within authority.
Draft the confirmation and obtain any required concession approval before sending.
Monitor due dates and report missed payments to the officer.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer leads every negotiation; the Finance Director or authorised delegate approves concessions beyond the officer's mandate.
systems: Excel or a proposed deterministic schedule calculator
data_needed: Previous promises and actual payment behaviour
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier with approved terms, confirmation, approver and instalment schedule; forecast inputs shared with FP&A.

evidence.claim: Software can calculate payment schedules and prepare account briefs while a person retains negotiation authority.
The 25% labour saving and 1.2x agreement-cycle speedup are hypotheses; customer willingness remains the main constraint.

risks: Suggested arrangements could exceed authority or accidentally concede a disputed claim.
Optimising collection pressure could harm customers and relationships; use factual, respectful approaches.
The O*NET references to returned merchandise and nonpayable checks are not established Noordhaven activities; focus on logistics invoices and evidenced claims.
research_questions: What authority does the officer have for instalments, interest waivers and settlements?
How much negotiation time is preparation and administration versus customer conversation and waiting?
Do proposed scenarios improve kept promises and cash forecast accuracy without increasing concessions?

tasks.short: Match Rabobank receipts to AFAS invoices and resolve payments that do not match.

today.trigger: A Rabobank statement or transaction feed becomes available.
steps: Import or review bank transactions in AFAS.
Match receipts to customer invoices using references and amounts.
Investigate partial payments, combined payments and missing references.
Post permitted allocations and leave unresolved receipts clearly identified.
Reconcile the bank and receivables position with accounts receivable.
drudgery: Searching invoice numbers in payment descriptions.
Adding invoice amounts to match combined receipts.
Requesting and interpreting remittance advice.
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous receipts and duplicate investigation between collections and the accounts-receivable Bookkeeper.

lenses.faster: Use AFAS bank matching for recognised transactions and extract invoice references from remittance advice for exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: A statement import triggers exact-match posting and reconciliation checks. Uncertain allocations enter a shared exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Keep unapplied cash low and give collections and FP&A an accurate view of which invoices are actually paid.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive matching and spend time solving the few receipts that need investigation.
lenses.options: Show candidate allocations with exact totals and supporting references instead of making an unexplained best guess.
lenses.altitude: I improve matching rules and remittance quality with the accounts-receivable Bookkeeper.
reach: Handle agreed cash-application exceptions for accounts receivable.
Provide receipt timing and unapplied-cash explanations to FP&A and the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Resolving ambiguous payer relationships, disputed deductions and allocations that could incorrectly close a customer's invoice.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank receipts, invoice references and balancing totals support deterministic matching and posting; an optional LLM step only extracts remittance details.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS receives a Rabobank statement through the configured connection or controlled import.
steps: Check statement completeness and reject duplicate transaction identifiers.
Run AFAS matching with approved reference, payer and amount rules.
Post unambiguous matches under configured permissions and reconcile control totals.
Extract references from remittance messages and present uncertain allocation candidates for approval.
Assign unresolved receipts to one owner and update collections only after posting succeeds.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve ambiguous and cross-customer allocations; refunds, write-offs and changes to customer bank details follow separate controls.
data_needed: Bank transaction IDs, dates, amounts and descriptions
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank journal and allocation history, linked to statement IDs; exception decisions and reconciliation totals in the shared queue.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports automatically importing bank statements and matching recognised lines to open items or ledger accounts.
Extracting remittance references can assist exceptions, provided arithmetic and posting decisions remain controlled.
The 75% labour saving and 3.5x processing speedup require substantial remaining manual work; gains will be smaller if AFAS matching is already well configured.

risks: A valid amount match can still allocate cash to the wrong customer or invoice.
Duplicate imports or partial failures can cause duplicate posting unless transaction IDs and reconciliation totals are checked.
Savings overlap with Bookkeeper work if ownership is unclear; count each receipt once and keep posting authority separate from refunds.
research_questions: What percentage of receipts does AFAS already match without intervention?
Which exception categories account for most handling time and allocation errors?
Can the Rabobank feed, AFAS posting controls and duplicate detection support unattended exact matches?
Who owns cash application today, and how will benefits be divided without double counting?

tasks.short: Keep customer addresses and contacts correct, and close inactive accounts under retention rules.

today.trigger: A customer reports a change, mail is returned, or an account becomes inactive.
steps: Identify the correct customer and verify the requested change.
Check outstanding balances, active disputes and the account's legal identity.
Update approved contact or address details in AFAS.
Archive or deactivate eligible accounts while retaining required records.
Notify relevant finance colleagues and preserve the change history.
drudgery: Rekeying address and contact details.
Finding duplicate customer records.
Checking retention conditions account by account.
today.time_sinks: Verifying changes and separating obsolete contact details from accounting records that must remain available.

lenses.faster: Extract proposed changes from messages and show a before-and-after comparison with validation results.
lenses.autonomous: Run scheduled checks for missing contacts, duplicates and retention review dates. Verified low-risk updates can eventually run by exception.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain reliable billing contacts across all sites and reduce overdue invoices caused by preventable delivery failures.
lenses.joy: Remove rekeying and repetitive checks, leaving identity problems and sensitive closures to investigate.
lenses.options: Compare updating, deactivating, merging or retaining an account, with the reason each option is allowed.
lenses.altitude: I own customer-data quality rules and monitor whether they reduce failed invoices and reminders.
reach: Support customer master-data maintenance for the Bookkeepers.
Coordinate finance retention reviews with the Controller and privacy owner.

tasks.human_edge: Confirming legal identity and handling sensitive closures without changing the debtor or losing evidence of an outstanding claim.
tasks.pattern_why: Proposed changes can be extracted and checked, but identity changes, merges and deletion decisions have consequences that require approval.

in_practice.trigger: A change request arrives or a scheduled data-quality review identifies an account.
steps: Extract proposed changes and display the existing and requested values.
Verify the request through an approved contact route and check whether the legal entity changes.
Check open balances, disputes, legal holds and the applicable retention category.
Obtain approval and write permitted changes through a validated AFAS route.
Retain the required historical record and report failed or conflicting updates.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve master-data changes during the pilot; legal-entity changes, merges, deceased sole-trader cases and deletion always need an authorised reviewer.
data_needed: Open balances, disputes and legal holds
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history and a restricted approval register with before-and-after values, verification evidence and retention decision.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents connectors for organisations, persons and sales relationships; exact writable fields need validation in Noordhaven's environment.
The 55% labour saving and 2x processing speedup assume routine changes dominate the workload.

risks: A fraudulent change request could redirect financial correspondence; bank-detail changes need a separate verification process.

Deletion must respect fiscal retention and historical master-data requirements. Dutch tax guidance identifies seven-year retention for basic accounting records. [Belastingdienst guidance](https://download.belastingdienst.nl/belastingdienst/docs/geautomatiseerde_administratie_en_fiscale_bewaarplicht_al0401z12fd.pdf)

AVG/GDPR also requires a justified retention schedule for personal data; do not retain every contact indefinitely. [AP guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/nl/over-privacy/persoonsgegevens/bewaren-van-persoonsgegevens)
Most customers are assumed to be businesses; the O*NET reference to deceased customers is relevant only where an individual customer or sole trader is involved.
research_questions: How many changes concern contact details versus legal identity, bank details or account closure?
Does AFAS preserve the historical values needed for financial audit and tax inspection?
Is there an approved retention schedule covering accounting records, correspondence and personal contact data?
Can proposed changes be verified without trusting the requesting message alone?

tasks.short: Prepare overdue accounts for an approved service hold or referral to a collection lawyer.

today.trigger: A material account remains unpaid after follow-up or repeatedly breaks payment agreements.
steps: Review outstanding amounts, disputes and previous collection attempts.
Gather invoices, agreements, correspondence and available delivery evidence.
Discuss the account with the Finance Director and relevant commercial or operations owner.
Obtain a decision on further contact, a service hold or external referral.
Send the approved case pack and monitor subsequent action.
drudgery: Compiling case packs from scattered records.
Writing collection chronologies.
Chasing approvals and external status updates.
today.time_sinks: Missing evidence, unclear decision ownership and repeated checking that the balance remains unpaid.

lenses.faster: Assemble a sourced chronology and case pack, then highlight missing documents before the approval meeting.
lenses.autonomous: Rules flag escalation candidates and prepare internal review tasks. Holds, referrals and external transmission require approval.
lenses.ambitious: Make every escalation decision evidence-based and compare expected recovery, cost and operational consequences.
lenses.joy: Replace document assembly and approval chasing with judgement about the best route to resolution.
lenses.options: Compare continued collection, a payment arrangement, legal referral and a proposed service hold with their costs and dependencies.
lenses.altitude: I manage escalation quality and recovery outcomes rather than assembling each dossier from scratch.
reach: Prepare doubtful-debt review packs for the Controller.
Coordinate approved collection-lawyer cases for the Finance Director.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether escalation is proportionate, contractually justified and commercially sensible when stopping logistics services could have wider consequences.
tasks.pattern_why: Evidence assembly and approval routing span several systems, while service interruption and legal referral require accountable human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An account crosses an approved escalation threshold or the officer requests review.
steps: Recheck the current balance, disputed amounts and prior notices.
Compile invoices, agreements and a source-linked collection chronology, marking missing evidence.
Prepare options with estimated recovery, cost and operational dependencies.
Route the pack to the authorised finance decision-maker and relevant commercial or operations owner.
After approval, transmit the permitted pack or issue the internal hold instruction and track acknowledgement.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director or authorised delegate approves every referral and service-hold decision; legal counsel checks disputed rights before action.
systems: Outlook or the external provider's approved secure channel
data_needed: Dispute records and available delivery evidence
Approval authority, provider details and operational dependencies
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted escalation register and AFAS dossier with evidence version, decision, approver, transmitted files and acknowledgement.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports adding dossier-workflow reactions and advancing workflow steps through an authorised connector.
Source-linked chronology drafting and completeness checks can assist preparation while people retain escalation authority.
The 45% labour saving and 1.6x internal escalation-cycle speedup are estimates; external legal recovery time is not assumed to improve.

risks: A missing dispute or recent payment could cause an unjustified referral or service interruption.
No transport or warehouse control system was supplied; service holds need an acknowledged instruction to an authorised operations owner.
Stored customer goods are not assumed to be available for repossession; any retention, release or enforcement action needs contractual and legal review.

An ordinary collection agency cannot use enforcement powers such as seizure. Choose the appropriate legal route and provider. [RVO collection guidance](https://ondernemersplein.overheid.nl/geldzaken-en-belastingen/cashflow/stappenplan-klant-betaalt-factuur-niet/)
research_questions: Who can approve service holds and external referrals, and what thresholds apply?
Are contracts, notices and delivery evidence complete enough to support a defensible case pack?
How will operations confirm a hold is applied, reviewed and released?
Does automated preparation reduce internal cycle time without increasing rejected or incomplete referrals?

role.altitude: Own the receivables exception process: accurate account histories, reliable collection priorities, credible payment commitments and evidenced escalation decisions.
reach: Take agreed cash-application exceptions from the accounts-receivable Bookkeepers.
Provide FP&A with payment promises, receipt scenarios and explanations of collection risk.
Prepare aged-receivables and doubtful-debt evidence for the Controller.
Coordinate recurring billing and delivery-evidence problems with finance and site operations.
Maintain customer contact-quality and collection-policy controls.
role.ceiling_note: The supplied tasks total 929.2 hours, about 58% of a 1,600-hour role. Applying the proposed labour-saving percentages yields about 489 hours annually, roughly 31% of the full role and EUR 22,000 of gross capacity at EUR 45/hour. This is released capacity, not a cash saving or a staffing recommendation; implementation, review and running costs are excluded. Current workflows are inferred from the supplied systems, and all savings and speedups require measurement. Speedups cover each task's operational cycle, not the eventual time until customers pay. Do not add overlapping Bookkeeper savings. Customer negotiation, disputed claims, operational dependencies and approval authority limit further autonomy.
skills_to_grow: Configure and test AFAS collection, dossier and bank-matching rules.
Measure handling time, exception rates and incorrect reminders against a baseline.
Check model-generated notes and explanations against original evidence.
Understand cash forecasting, receivables ageing and doubtful-debt evidence.
Strengthen negotiation, dispute resolution and commercial judgement.
Apply customer-data access and retention rules; keep AFAS HR and payroll data outside collection workflows.
Assess EU AI Act implications before adding AI creditworthiness assessment of natural persons. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)

Involve the OR where new employee-data or monitoring arrangements require consent; customer collection automation alone does not establish that requirement. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/aan-de-slag-met-de-or/rechten/instemmingsrecht)
role.ambitious_version: Run a receivables operation in which routine records, exact payment matches and approved reminders flow automatically. Use the released time to resolve disputes before close, improve customer payment commitments and give FP&A an evidence-based weekly cash outlook. Measure success through lower DSO, fewer unapplied receipts, accurate promise-based forecasts and fewer receivables adjustments at month close.
